metaTitle: Akwasidae at Manhyia Palace, Kumasi: Dates and What to Expect
metaDescription: Akwasidae is the Asante festival held every six weeks on a Sunday, when the Asantehene sits in state at Manhyia Palace in Kumasi. How the cycle works, what happens and how to go.
ogTitle: Akwasidae: the Asantehene sits in state
subtitle: The Asantehene sits in state, every six weeks
answer: Akwasidae is the Asante festival that comes round every six weeks on a Sunday, following the 42-day Akan calendar. On the day the Asantehene, the king of Asante, sits in state at Manhyia Palace in Kumasi, receiving chiefs and visitors amid drumming, horn-blowing and dancing, after rites for the ancestors. It is one of the most accessible royal ceremonies in Ghana.

sections.title: When is Akwasidae?
sections.html:
The Akan calendar runs in cycles of six weeks, and Akwasidae falls on a Sunday at the end of each, so there are eight or nine a year.[[1,2]] In 2026 they fell on 1 February, 15 March, 26 April, 7 June, 19 July, 30 August, 11 October and 22 November; the next is on 3 January 2027.[[3]]

The last Akwasidae of the Asante year is Adae Kese, the biggest, with offerings of food and gifts to people in need.[[1]]

sections.title: What happens
sections.html: Before the public ceremony the Asantehene performs rites for the ancestors, including a visit to the royal mausoleum at Bantama.[[4]] Then he sits in state at Manhyia, carried in a palanquin with drummers, dancers and horn-blowers, and chiefs, dignitaries and visitors come forward to greet him.[[4]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Manhyia Palace is in Kumasi; the Manhyia Palace Museum is on the same grounds.
Visitors: it is a formal royal occasion, but visitors are welcome. Dress respectfully and follow the palace officials.
Photos: ask before photographing the Asantehene or the rites.
Check first: confirm the date locally; an Akwasidae near Christmas may be moved or cancelled.
While you’re there: Kejetia market and the Kente villages of Bonwire and Adanwomase are close. See the Ashanti region page.

faq.a: An Asante festival held every six weeks on a Sunday, when the Asantehene sits in state at Manhyia Palace in Kumasi to receive chiefs and visitors.
Every 42 days, at the end of each six-week cycle of the Akan calendar, always on a Sunday.
Yes. It is a formal royal occasion, but visitors are welcome if they dress and behave respectfully.
The last and biggest Akwasidae of the Asante year.
